name: Weak guesstimate: tennis balls in a 747 with no scoping, unit error three orders of magnitude off, no sanity check

messages.text: How many tennis balls could fit inside a Boeing 747?
Okay, a 747 is big. I think it is about 70 meters long, and inside maybe 6 meters wide and 6 meters high. So 70 times 6 times 6 is 2,520 cubic meters.
Okay. What are you including in that space?
Just the inside of the plane, all of it. Then a tennis ball is about 10 centimeters, so that is 0.1, so one ball is 0.1 cubic meters. 2,520 divided by 0.1 is 25,200 tennis balls.
What about the seats, galleys, the cargo hold? And the gaps between balls?
I think it is fine to ignore the seats, you could take them out. The gaps are small. I will keep it at about 25,000.
Does 25,000 feel right to you? Think about a smaller space you know.
Yeah it feels okay, it is a lot of balls. A plane is big but balls are also kind of big.
Anything you would change, or what drives the answer most?
Not really, I think 25,000 is my answer. Maybe a bit more or less.
